blurb: Chinese number code for "I love you"; May 20 is an online Valentine's Day
title: 520 Meaning: What 520, 521 and 1314 Mean in Chinese
description: 520 means "I love you" in Chinese number slang. 521 means "I do", 1314 "forever", and 5201314 "I love you forever". May 20 is a love day.
answer: 520 is Chinese number slang for "I love you" (我爱你): 5-2-0, read wǔ èr líng, sounds close to wǒ ài nǐ. 521 is usually read as "I'm willing" or "I love you", 1314 (yī sān yī sì) sounds like 一生一世, "for a lifetime", and 5201314 together means "I love you forever". That is why May 20 and 21 have become an unofficial online Valentine's Day in China.

body: Writing feelings as digits is an old habit of Chinese chat: numbers are quick to type and a little coy, so a string of them can say what people find awkward to say outright.

The use of 520 for "I love you" is often traced to the 1998 song 数字恋爱 (Digital Love) by Taiwanese singer Mavis Fan (范晓萱). It spread widely online, and May 20 gradually became a day for confessions, gifts, weddings and 520-themed sales. The holiday has no official founding date.

body: On WeChat, the cap on a single personal red envelope rises from the usual 200 yuan to 520 yuan for May 20 only, so sending exactly 520 or 1314 yuan is a popular gesture between couples.
Because 520 and 1314 read as love messages, avoid them as amounts when paying a coworker or client back; round to another number instead.
Among close friends 520 can be a playful "love ya" with no romance intended, so read it in context.

faq.q: What is the difference between 520 and 521?
faq.a: Both can mean "I love you". 521 is also read as "I'm willing" (我愿意) and is often used to answer someone's 520.
1314 sounds like 一生一世, "for one whole lifetime". It is usually paired with 520 as 5201314, "I love you forever".

faq.q: Is May 20 an official holiday in China?
faq.a: No. It is an internet-born "Valentine's Day" that many couples celebrate, not a public holiday.
